description.narrative:
Heavy rainfalls are causing severe flooding all across northern Nigeria, so far affecting 31 states and over 1 million individuals. Borno State in the northeast is among the most affected states, with over 414,000 people severely affected, 400,000 people displaced, 37 people reported dead, and 58 people injured. When the recent flash floods broke out in Borno State, northeast Nigeria was already facing an acute food crisis and an ongoing conflict with non-state armed forces. The flash floods in Borno state, caused by heavy rainfalls and aggravated by the breaking of the Alau Dam in Konduga Local Government Area (LGA), have caused extensive damage to infrastructure, crops and shelter, severely impacting livelihoods and displacing households.
According to the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), the fast-moving waters submerged over 70% of Maiduguri city. OCHA estimates that over 400,000 people in Borno State were displaced, forcing them to relocate to former and operational IDP camps already housing IDPs. Former and operational IDPs camps quickly reached full-capacity, unable to provide safe-drinking water, food, and basic NFIs to recently displaced populations.

SUMMARY The Dutch Relief Alliance has activated its fastest crisis response mechanism to develop an emergency humanitarian response within 72-hours to assist flood-affected populations in North-East Nigeria (Borno State). Six Dutch based NGOs (Plan International, Oxfam, CARE, Terre des Hommes, ZOA & Stichting Vluchteling/IRC) together with seven local NGOs (CHAD, CRUDAN, CATAI, CBI, EYN, LABDI, LHI & GHV Africa) have joined hands to provide emergency relief including access to safe drinking water, in order to prevent illnesses like cholera, providing food and financial assistance to replace belongings lost during the floods, as well as emergency protection services such as assisting children who have lost their families. At least 130.000 people will be supported with such assistance.

The total number of individuals targeted, without double counting, is 13,440. Vulnerable groups include recently displaced HHs, female-headed households, PLWs, women at risk of GBV, households with persons with disabilities, child-headed households or UASC, as well as households headed by elderly or sick persons.

WASH: The JR aims to improve access to safe drinking water, improve (safe) access to WASH facilities, prevent waterborne diseases and improve public health outcomes. WASH activities have been devised to also address the most pressing public health concerns, including water-borne diseases and water contamination. Activities include distributing water purification tablets, distributing dignity/hygiene kits, providing emergency water trucking, repairing, disinfecting and rehabilitating water points, rehabilitating latrines or installing emergency latrines, as well as conducting culturally sensitive health and hygiene promotion. Plan and its partner CHAD, and SV/IRC will provide emergency water trucking aiming to immediately enable access to at least 15l/pp/day of clean water to people still living in IDP camps, or in communities already returning to areas where water systems have been damaged. ZOA, Oxfam, Terre des Hommes, Plan International and SV/IRC will disinfect and rehabilitate boreholes (water points) destroyed by the floods, in coordination with the Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency for technical support and maintenance. Terre des Hommes and ZOA will both replace or repair latrines, ensuring they are safe and gender-segregated, fully equipped with handwashing stations and drainage systems. Hygiene and dignity kits, containing soap, laundry soap towels, toothpaste, brush, soap, jerrycan, reusable hygiene pads and kettle will be distributed by ZOA, Plan, SV/IRC and Oxfam. The joint response will also include health and hygiene promotion as well as training of promoters.
MPC: ZOA, Oxfam and Plan will provide multipurpose cash assistance (MPC) in order to address the nutrition, food, shelter and non-food items (NFI) needs of the affected population. MPC was identified in partners’ rapid need assessment as an appropriate response in order to stimulate markets, which are slowly recuperating, and enable households to prioritise their most urgent needs. Partners will align with the local CWG guidelines and MEB. ZOA, together with partners LHI and CBI will provide one round of MPC, supporting 1300 HHs (6500 persons). Oxfam aims to provide MPC to 14,000 individuals, leveraging ongoing initiatives to maximise impacts. Plan will provide monthly MPC over a 3-month period to 900 vulnerable households (7,200 individuals) to improve the nutritional status of households, particularly children under-5, pregnant and lactating women and the elderly, and to allow HHs to replace key lost assets. MPC is an important component aimed at addressing the lack of access to food commodities.
FSL: CARE will provide direct food assistance, distributing two hot meals (wet feeding) per day for 10 days to 6,000 people still in IDP camps, in addition to cash for food for 300HH. The response will target families in flood-affected areas through participatory targeting in coordination with other partners in the target locations to prevent overlaps, promote inclusivity, and ensure assistance reaches the appropriate deserving participants based on vulnerability.
Protection: Plan, Care and Terre des Hommes will provide protection services in order to reach the most vulnerable children and adolescents, including those with disabilities. Activities include setting up case management for child protection and SGBV. Case management will also entail the identification and reunification of UASC as well as specialized services for children with disabilities. Considering the increasing risks of SBGV, partners will carry out SGBV awareness campaigns, ensuring that they are culturally appropriate and inclusive. Terre des Hommes will also establish community-based protection mechanisms, which include CP Protection Focal Points, child rights groups, and Women & Men Against SGBV groups, which will serve as first responders, identify protection concerns and refer to appropriate services. Psychosocial support will be provided through child-friendly spaces, as well as women and girl’s safe spaces.
Nutrition: With 40% of beds in stabilization centres affected by the flooding, this joint response via SV/IRC will aim to rehabilitate the Mashamari Stabilization Center through the procurement of laboratory equipment, oxygen concentrators, essential drugs, and therapeutic food, as well as additional bedding and mattresses. SV/IRC is also aiming to establish integrated nutrition treatment centers in IDP camps.
Shelter/NFI: Approximately 10500 beneficiaries will also be provided with jerrycans, buckets, soap, cooking items, solar torchlights and other items in the first weeks of the crisis to meet urgent needs.
